checks: Exact named synthetic native tests; paired syntax projection
cost: O(bytes+lines*metadata keys+lines*headings) parse/body/items checks can be quadratic in line/headings counts; bib parse delegated, temporary strings O(bytes). No filesystem effects.
description: parse stores lines, toggles fence state, collects first machine metadata block with first case-insensitive key, then detects ATX/setext/caps/bare changelog outside fence/meta. body ends at next same-or-higher heading or metadata start. items scans paragraphs/lists, bib brace depth capped at 80 lines, and unmarked reference starts after period with year/word/case guards. docs_page strips exact Jekyll markers/front matter and statistics suffix.
forward: parse stores lines, toggles fence state, collects first machine metadata block with first case-insensitive key, then detects ATX/setext/caps/bare changelog outside fence/meta. body ends at next same-or-higher heading or metadata start. items scans paragraphs/lists, bib brace depth capped at 80 lines, and unmarked reference starts after period with year/word/case guards. docs_page strips exact Jekyll markers/front matter and statistics suffix.
inverse: Readme retains line texts modulo CR endings, while section/item projections lose whitespace and markers; raw and text item representations define different fibers. Metadata alone cannot reconstruct duplicate keys or full document.
Fenced lines cannot become headings; first metadata duplicate wins case-insensitively. However items only skips fence delimiters, so fenced bodies may still become items.
limitations: Partial source models and finite fixtures only. No corpus/model/network/site/release execution or universal proof.
state: Bounded helper inputs and source-derived CLI state/effects; see catalog.
